title.narrative: Recognising and Enabling Environmental Defenders to Halt Deforestation

description.narrative: Global Witness and Consortium partners, representing indigenous peoples' civil society groups in Brazil and Colombia, are working together to achieve NICFI’s aim to reduce and reverse tropical forest loss by exposing its financial and supply chain drivers, advancing rights-based, inclusive forest governance, and protecting land, environmental defenders (LEDs). To do this, our project will focus on four key objectives - 1) Protection: LEDs in Brazil and Colombia are better protected from threats and attacks and can therefore advocate for their rights and focus on their livelihoods and territorial governance. 2) Equipped: LEDs are better equipped to protect their rights and forest territories through improved access to resources, data generation, and are strengthened with advocacy and documentation skills to act on this information. 3) Advocacy: Governments, oversight institutions, and international/regional decision-makers, regulators and policy bodies are pressured by LED evidence and advocacy to adopt and enforce rights-based laws, standards and agreements that reduce deforestation, restrict harmful finance and uphold the rights and safety of defenders. 4) Recognition: LEDs are increasingly, publicly and politically, recognised as legitimate forest protectors, while also recognising and connecting with each other’s struggles, and actively participate as key actors in ending tropical forest loss, with their knowledge, experiences and proposed solutions meaningfully considered in decision-making. Through these objectives we want to contribute to the reduction in Tropical Forest loss because forests are better protected by LEDs, including Indigenous Peoples, who are better protected, better recognised, better equipped, and more influential. LEDs have the agency, resources and legitimacy to continue their work, protect their territories, influence policy and enforcement from community to global level.
